messages.content: Write a polished short scene in modern American English between two adult friends who both know there is something awkward between them after a recent misunderstanding. Let the discomfort show through pauses, careful wording, small actions, and attempts at normal conversation. Do not explain every feeling directly. Let them gradually find their normal rhythm again without a dramatic speech or complete resolution.

Sam set the takeout menu on the table. “You still want Thai?”

Riley looked at it. “Sure.”

“You said you wanted pizza.”

“I did.”

A pause.

“Thai is fine.”

“Okay.”

Sam reached for the phone, then stopped. “You pick.”

“You always pick.”

“That’s not true.”

“It is.”

Sam looked at her. “You really want to argue about noodles?”

Riley almost smiled. “No.”

“Good.”

Another quiet stretch followed. Riley folded and unfolded the corner of the menu.

“You can just say it,” she said.

Sam leaned back. “Say what?”

“That you’re still annoyed.”

“I am.”

Riley nodded. “Okay.”

“I also don’t want to spend all night being annoyed.”

She glanced over. “That seems reasonable.”

“Thank you.”

“You’re welcome.”

Sam handed her the phone. “Pick the food.”

Riley looked at the screen. “Pad thai?”

“Yeah.”

“Extra peanuts?”

Sam smiled. “There you are.”

Riley gave him a look. “Don’t ruin it.”

“I wouldn’t dare.”
